Before signing a CMMC preparation proposal, ask what happens after the findings report arrives.

Who implements the changes? What does your internal team need to provide? What evidence will be available when the work is reviewed?

Those questions turn a broad promise of “readiness” into a service you can evaluate. Ask a prospective provider to explain one example deliverable using sanitized material, without disclosing another customer's information. Then compare the proposed work with your environment and internal capacity.

We at Cloud2e provide CMMC preparation support that includes gap assessment, technical remediation and documentation. The practical value is connecting identified gaps with implementation work and records that explain the result.

Our new provider-selection guide offers questions to bring into that discussion. Use the same questions with us.

A useful proposal should make responsibilities, deliverables and ongoing support clear. A promised assessment outcome cannot substitute for those details.

Compare CMMC preparation providers by what their proposals make clear.

A scope of work should explain the environment being addressed, the deliverables, the remediation responsibilities and the support available after the initial project. Ask where advisory work ends and implementation begins.

Cloud2e's CMMC preparation services include gap assessment, remediation and System Security Plan, POA&M and policy documentation support. These are service areas to discuss against your needs, rather than assume every proposal includes the same work.

Bring three questions to your next provider conversation: Who performs the engineering? What records document the work? Who maintains the environment and documentation afterward?

Also ask how the preparation engagement relates to a separate, independent assessment. No preparation provider should promise the assessor's decision.

Our Insights guide explains practical questions for choosing a provider. Use it to compare responsibilities and deliverables before comparing price alone.
